annotationMethod: Independent Astra Max source-only visual review and native pixel ROI verification. Projected pelvis/torso X is chosen separately from support ROI X. Root Y reproduces exclusive alpha>=64 support extent. Fresh per-army contact cap-to-near-sole half-up median is shared unchanged with its casualty partner; no phase-height normalization.

groundMethods: Projected pelvis X is independent of the support-foot X. Ground Y is the alpha>=64 exclusive bottom of the nearer viewer-left/rear boot, isolated below its trouser cuff.
Projected pelvis X follows the hips behind the extended torso and forearm. Ground Y comes from the nearer viewer-left/rear supporting boot sole, without weapon pixels.
Projected pelvis X follows the withdrawn torso/hips. Ground Y comes from the nearer viewer-left boot sole under the rear supporting leg.
Projected pelvis X follows the hips in the widened low guard. Ground Y comes from the nearer viewer-left/rear boot sole; it is separate from weapon and farther-foot bounds.
Projected pelvis X follows the initial backward hit/stumble. Ground Y is the nearer viewer-right boot sole, isolated from the loosely held rifle and other foot.
Projected lower-torso/hip X is independent of the planted foot. Ground Y is the near planted sole segment below the bent leg; the raised rear boot and released rifle stock are excluded.
Projected lower-torso/hip X follows the forward collapse. Ground Y is the lowered blue-trouser knee support edge. The backward-facing raised boot soles and separate rifle are excluded.
Projected torso/hip X represents the resting body. Ground Y is the lower navy coat/hip edge touching the implied ground, isolated from the separate rifle and the far-forward arms.
Projected pelvis X is chosen between the anatomical hips rather than from the rifle-inclusive bounds. Ground Y is the nearer viewer-right planted boot sole, isolated below the trouser cuff.
Projected pelvis X follows the hips behind the SW extension. Ground Y is the forward viewer-left planted boot sole; the lifted/farther opposite foot is excluded.
Projected pelvis X follows the hips during withdrawal. Ground Y is the nearer viewer-right boot sole, independent of the low rifle.
Projected pelvis X follows the torso/hips under the across-body block. Ground Y is the nearer viewer-right boot sole; the other boot and bayonet are excluded.
Projected pelvis X follows the hips during the initial hit/stumble. Ground Y is the nearer viewer-right boot sole, separated from the bayonet that reaches farther down the cell.
Projected lower-torso/hip X is independent of the forward support hand. Ground Y is the near palm/fingertip contact during knee-down, excluding rifle and farther boot.
Projected lower-torso/hip X follows the collapsing body. Ground Y is the forward near-hand knuckle contact; the rifle and tucked knee are excluded.

Projected torso/hip X represents the resting body. Ground Y is a narrow visible gray elbow/forearm support edge behind the rifle, with a transparent gap below inside the ROI; brown stock pixels are excluded.
